Subject: Workload fingerprint and initial sizing ask

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the call earlier — attaching the workload fingerprint export you asked for (hightower_workload_fingerprint.csv). High-level summary:~

- Production traffic: ~4.5M API requests / month (~150k/day)
- Model: mix of open 70B-family (long context) and a trimmed 13B for cheaper batch jobs
- Average prompt tokens: 1,200; avg completion tokens: 600 (many long-form summaries)
- Peak concurrent inference requests (1-min peaks): ~120 concurrent requests
- SLA target: p50 < 250ms for short prompts, p95 < 1,200ms acceptable for long-context jobs
- Primary region: us-west

We want a recommended dedicated pool (GPU type & count), suggested reserved commit level (monthly USD), and options for burst/bandwidth (we expect spikes during business hours).

Can you share a concise sizing recommendation and packaging options (committed tier, burst credits, and any quantization/partitioning suggestions) by EOD next week? Procurement is on cc to help with timing.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Li

High-level notes from the fingerprint: we see heavy long-context usage and a non-trivial number of concurrent requests which pushes toward faster GPUs and KV-cache strategies.

We’ll come back with two packaging options: 1) latency-first (smaller pool of H100s, higher commit) and 2) cost-first (larger mix with quantized 13B fallbacks + burst credit).

I expect we’ll attach a first-pass proposal PDF and a short sizing spreadsheet. Will follow up tomorrow with numbers.

Emma / Grace / Ben — attached is a first-pass sizing sheet (sizing-sheet.xlsx) and a short proposal (redwood_pool_proposal_v1.pdf). Key recommendations summarized below so procurement can review quickly: 

Recommended baseline (latency-first):
- GPU type: 8 x H100 80GB (dedicated pool)
- Effective capacity: sized for ~120 concurrent long-context requests with p95 under 1.1s using KV-cache + optimized kernels
- Reserved commit (monthly USD): $120,000 (gives predictable throughput and 15% discount vs pay-as-you-go)
- Burst capacity: +2x burst credits for 4 hours/day (auto-billed overage at reduced burst rate)
- Fallthrough model mix: keep a smaller quantized 13B pool (3 x A100-80GB quantized) for non-real-time batch tasks to save cost

Alternative (cost-first):
- GPU type: 5 x H100 + 6 x quantized 13B A100 instances (hybrid pool)
- Reserved commit (monthly USD): $85,000 (larger reliance on quantized path reduces commit)
- Expected 20–30% higher p95 for long-form prompts but ~30% lower monthly cost

Operational notes / optimizations:
- We recommend enabling prefix/KV-cache for your long-form summarization flows — this reduces repeated prompt token computation and improves effective throughput by ~1.7x for sessions with repeated context.
- Model pinning: keep production traffic pinned to a specific model version; allow automatic fallback to quantized variants when pool utilization exceeds 85%.

Next steps:
1) Emma/procurement to confirm priority (latency vs cost) and any hard constraints on monthly commit.
2) If latency-first chosen, we’ll prepare an SOW + draft contract with the $120k commit and burst terms.

Notes attached: sizing assumptions are documented in the sizing-sheet. Happy to run an onsite benchmark if helpful.

—Marissa

1) Can you include an explicit SLA for p99 tail behavior for the long-context path? We can tolerate slightly higher p95, but p99 hits need a clear mitigation (fallback model + throttling policy).
2) Please include the 20% committed discount and 60 days of burst credits in the draft SOW.
3) We want a migration window: one week of cold-run testing with telemetry access to Redwood Console and a post-migration tuning session (2 hours) with Marissa’s team.

If you can send the SOW + MSA redline by EOD Thursday we’ll target signature the following week.
